name: Maria Helena Moraes Scripilliti
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2014-2022); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Maria Helena Moraes Scripilliti's late father, Jose Ermirio de Moraes, founded family-owned Grupo Votorantim, one of Brazil's largest conglomerates.
Votorantim operates in more than 20 countries in the aluminum, pulp and paper, energy, agribusiness, and cement industries.
The group dates back to 1918, when Moraes Scripilliti's father bought a textile factory in Sao Paulo.
The family still controls 100% of the business. Maria Helena's brother, Ermirio Pereira, is also a billionaire.
Moraes Scripilliti's late husband, Clovis Scripilliti, helped expand Votorantim throughout northeast Brazil during the 1960s and 1970s.
forbes_facts: Her brother Antonio Ermirio ran to become governor of Sao Paulo, Brazil's richest state.  He did not win. He died in 2014.

name: Harish Ahuja
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Hurun India (2018-2019)
forbes_bio: Harish Ahuja is chairman of Shahi Exports, an Indian apparel manufacturer and exporter operating across eight Indian states, including Karnataka and Haryana.
It has 50 manufacturing units and three processing mills across eight Indian states.
The company is a big employer of women, who account for 70% of its workforce of 100,000 people.
The company's marquee list of clients includes international brands such Calvin Klein, Gap and H&M.
forbes_facts: His son Anand is married to Bollywood actress Sonam Kapoor.
Shahi Exports was founded in 1974 by his mother Sarla Ahuja.
In September 2024, he bought a home in London's Notting Hill for $27 million.

name: Chang Kuo-Hua
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun China (2008-2026)
forbes_bio: Chang Kuo-Hua is the oldest son of shipping tycoon Chang Yung Fa, who died in 2016 at the age of 88.
In 1968 Yung Fa founded Evergreen Marine, now one of the world's largest transportation companies.
Brothers Kuo-Hua, Kuo-Ming and Kuo-Cheng also inherited stakes in EVA Airways and hotels in Taiwan, mainland China, Paris and Bangkok.
Kuo-Hua sits on the board of Evergreen Marine.

name: Song Zuowen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2022); Hurun China (2010-2021)
forbes_bio: Song Zuowen's privately-held Nanshan Group has interests in aluminum, apparel, education, tourism and a regional airline.
It listed its main aluminum company, Shandong Nanshan Aluminum, on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 1999.
Nanshan Group is the majority investor in startup Qingdao Airlines, which launched in April 2014.

name: Shmuel Harlap
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Shmuel Harlap is the chairman and part owner of Colmobil, Israel's largest car importer, which his father acquired in 1962.
He is also an active investor who put $10,000 into automotive tech startup Mobileye in 2001 and eventually acquired a 7.2% stake.
Intel purchased Mobileye for $15.3 billion in cash in 2017, netting Harlap $750 million from the deal, which made him a billionaire.
Harlap continues to invest in Israeli startups, particularly in the cybersecurity, nanotechnology and life sciences industries.
forbes_facts: While Harlap was fighting in the Six-Day War, his father was persuading Mercedes-Benz to deliver 1,625 trucks to Israel to move supplies.
Harlap has a Ph.D from Harvard in political philosophy.

name: Abel Avellan
sec_insider_companies: AST SpaceMobile, Inc. (ASTS) - Chief Executive Officer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Abel Avellan is the founder and CEO of AST SpaceMobile, which is building satellites that enable broadband connections directly to cell phones.
Avellan was born in Venezuela, where he trained as an engineer. After college, we went to work for Swedish communications giant Ericsson.
Avellan founded his first company, Emerging Markets Communications in 2000, which provided satellite communications to remote places.
He sold Emerging Markets Communications in 2016 for $550 million, and used his share of the proceeds to found AST.
AST SpaceMobile has contracts with Verizon, AT&T and Vodafone to provide connections to customers in areas without tower coverage.

name: Igor Rotenberg
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Igor Rotenberg is the son of billionaire Arkady Rotenberg, a close friend of Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Rotenberg, once a junior partner in his father's business, used to control drilling company Gazprom Burenie and collected dividends from the company worth almost $560 million from 2017 until 2021, when he sold his shares.
He was also a shareholder in Platon Electronic Toll Collection system, which processes the collections of tolls for vehicles over 12 tons, and Aviapark, one of Europe's biggest shopping malls.
forbes_facts: After US Treasury Department imposed sanctions against his father in 2014, Rotenberg bought his father's stakes in some assets.
Rotenberg was once a top-manager of state-owned Russian Railways.

name: Ren Zhengfei
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2011-2022); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun China (2000-2026)
forbes_bio: Ren Zhengfei leads Huawei Technologies, one of the world's largest manufacturer of telecommunication hardware and mobile phones.
Ren is the son of school teachers and grew up in a mountainous town in southern China's Guizhou Province.
Ren held technician posts in China's military and worked for Shenzhen South Sea Oil before establishing Huawei with the equivalent of $3,000 in 1987.
Huawei today does business in more than 170 countries with 180,000 employees.

name: Sarah MacMillan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Sarah MacMillan owns an estimated 3% stake in Cargill, the largest food company in the world.
She is one of four billionaire sisters who inherited stakes in the company from their father W. Duncan MacMillan, who died in 2006.
Her great-great-grandfather, W.W. Cargill, founded the business as a single grain warehouse on the end of an Iowa railroad line in 1865.
The family still owns roughly 90% of Cargill, which did $154 billion in 2025 sales across food, agriculture, financial and industrial divisions.

name: Wilma Tisch
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2018)
forbes_bio: Wilma Tisch owes her fortune to her late husband Laurence (d. 2003) and his brother Bob, who started Loews Corp as a New Jersey hotel venture in 1946.
Wilma's son James is the president and CEO of  publicly traded Loews, which now has interests in drilling, natural gas pipelines and insurance.
Her sister-in law Joan Tisch, also a billionaire, died in 2017; Wilma's son Andrew co-chairs Loews' board with Joan's son Jonathan.
At NYU, the Tisch family donated funds to support the Tisch School of the Arts and the Tisch Hospital at Langone Medical Center.
Wilma donates some of her Loews shares annually to her three children's charitable foundations.
forbes_facts: Tisch was the first woman to be elected president of the Federation of Jewish Philanthropies of New York.
Tisch is an honorary board member of WNYC Radio and holds an honorary doctorate from NYU.

name: Liesel Pritzker Simmons
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Liesel Pritzker Simmons and her brother Matthew Pritzker sued their family for a chunk of its Hyatt Hotels fortune and received around $500 million apiece in 2005.
Their uncle Jay Pritzker (d. 1999) founded the hotel chain and their uncle Donald Pritzker (d. 1972) managed and developed it.
Their father Robert Pritzker (d. 2011) ran the family's industrial conglomerate Marmon Group, which was acquired by Berkshire Hathaway in a series of transactions beginning in 2008.
Three of Matthew and Liesel's step-siblings, seven cousins and their father's cousin Nick Pritzker are also billionaires.
Liesel cofounded and runs impact investing firm Blue Haven Initiative with her husband Ian Simmons.
forbes_facts: Pritzker, a child actor, starred in the 1995 film ?A Little Princess? as well as ?Air Force One? with Harrison Ford.

name: Silvana Armani
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Silvana Armani is the niece of billionaire fashion designer Giorgio Armani (d. September 2025) and the daughter of his late brother Sergio Armani.
She is a board member of Armani's namesake fashion firm and leads the womenswear division. She is also seen as her uncle's stylistic successor.
Under the terms of Armani's will, Silvana is entitled to 17% of the net proceeds from the sale or public listing of 45% of the company within five years of Armani's death.
She also inherited some of Armani's shares in eyewear giant EssilorLuxottica as well as a stake in Armani's superyacht and his empire of luxury homes.
